name: Garlic Butter Steak with Creamed Spinach
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so they come to room temperature. Pat dry and season well on both sides with salt and pepper.

Start the creamed spinach. Melt 20 g of the butter in a large, deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the brown onion for 3-4 minutes until soft, then add half the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the thickened cream and stir in the ground nutmeg. Simmer for 4-5 minutes until reduced by about a third and slightly thickened.
Stir in the cream cheese until melted and smooth, then add the baby spinach in big handfuls, letting each batch wilt into the sauce before adding the next.
Stir through the parmesan and a squeeze of juice from half the lemon. Season with salt and pepper, take off the heat and keep warm.
Heat a heavy frying pan over high heat until smoking hot. Add a splash of olive oil and sear the steaks for 2 minutes per side without moving them.

Turn the heat down to medium, then drop in the remaining 40 g butter and the rest of the garlic. Tilt the pan and spoon the foaming garlic butter over the steaks for 1-2 minutes, then pull them off at 52-54°C in the centre for medium-rare.
Rest the steaks for 5 minutes, then slice thickly. Serve on the creamed spinach with the pan butter spooned over and the remaining lemon cut into wedges.
